hero.headline: Trump administration officials address slush fund controversy
hero.teaser: Trump officials are working to calm Republican anger over a controversial Anti-Weaponization Fund that has stalled an immigration enforcement bill.
hero.body:
President Donald Trump may need to explicitly renounce his controversial Anti-Weaponization Fund before Republicans move forward with a stalled immigration enforcement bill. Trump administration officials are attempting to address the fury among congressional Republicans over the fund.

The fund, created following Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS over leaked tax return documents, establishes nearly $1.8 billion to be distributed to alleged victims of what the administration calls "lawfare." The justice department will administer the fund through four commissioners appointed by Trump's attorney general, plus one commissioner selected in consultation with congressional leadership. Trump retains the ability to fire the commissioners, giving him ultimate control over the fund's operations.

The fund will have authority to issue formal apologies for alleged mistreatment of conservative political figures by previous administrations. Legal experts and congressional critics from both parties have attacked the fund as a corrupt scheme they describe as a slush fund for Trump allies. Some have noted that January 6 insurrectionists may be eligible recipients, with some reportedly planning to apply for grants.

The controversy highlights significant tensions within the Republican party over the administration's financial priorities and use of federal resources. Some Republicans are demanding clarity on the fund before proceeding with other legislative initiatives. The dispute has become a roadblock to advancing immigration enforcement legislation that party members otherwise support.

Critics have raised concerns about the fund's lack of transparency. The fund's work is not required to be made public, and reports to the attorney general regarding its conduct must remain confidential. This opacity has drawn additional scrutiny from lawmakers concerned about accountability.

The agreement establishing the fund requires the IRS to drop all audits of Trump and his family. The justice department said it "disagrees strongly" with a recent court decision halting the fund's establishment, signaling the administration intends to continue defending the arrangement through legal channels.

Legal scholars have characterized the fund as problematic on multiple levels. They argue that because Trump effectively controlled both sides of the lawsuit against the IRS, a genuine conflict did not exist. A federal judge had commissioned an independent legal review, which found "reason to believe that the president is, in fact, exercising his control over the defendants in this litigation." The agreement was reached shortly before the judge's deadline requiring the parties to explain how they were actually in conflict.

The fund's establishment is part of a broader pattern that critics say demonstrates widespread self-dealing and conflicts of interest within the Trump administration. Beyond this particular controversy, legal experts worry the fund sets a problematic precedent for future administrations regarding the use of federal resources for personal or political purposes.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes 25% Tariff on Brazil
cards.teaser: The White House announced plans for new tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing trade practices it considers unfair.
cards.body:
President Trump proposed a 25% tariff on imports from Brazil, marking another step in the administration's use of trade barriers. The proposal cites what officials describe as unfair trade practices by Brazil.

The tariff plan relies on Section 301 investigations, a legal mechanism the administration has used to justify trade actions. The move represents the latest effort to rebuild the administration's tariff strategy following previous trade disputes.

cards.headline: Rubio testifies before Senate as Iran negotiations stall
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on the State Department budget request as negotiations to end the three-m.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on Tuesday morning regarding the State Department budget request. The hearing took place as negotiations to end the three-month war in Iran have stalled. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also appeared before Congress for budget hearings.

Rubio addressed lawmakers on the administration's approach to the Iran conflict and its broader foreign policy priorities during the proceedings.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran negotiations continuing despite complexity
cards.teaser: President Trump stated that talks with Iran remain active, describing the pursuit of a deal as a complicated process.
cards.body:
President Trump told Fox News that negotiations with Iran are ongoing, characterizing the effort to reach an agreement as a difficult undertaking. He dismissed suggestions that talks had stalled, saying a deal is not a simple thing to achieve.

The comments come as Trump reviews a proposed memorandum of understanding drafted by American and Iranian diplomats with assistance from Pakistan and Qatar. The preliminary agreement would continue the current ceasefire for 60 days while negotiations continue on a more permanent peace accord. Reports indicate Tehran has suspended discussions over Israeli military actions in Lebanon, though the White House continues pushing for a deal amid polling pressure and demands from Gulf allies.

cards.headline: Russian Strikes Kill 18 in Ukraine as Moscow Escalates After Military Setbacks
cards.body:
Russia unleashed a massive assault on Ukrainian cities overnight, launching 73 missiles and 656 drones across five major population centers. The coordinated attack killed at least 18 people and injured dozens more, with rescue workers continuing operations to pull bodies and survivors from collapsed buildings.

The strikes targeted Kyiv, the central cities of Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia, and the eastern cities of Poltava and Kharkiv. The Russian arsenal included eight hypersonic Tsirkon missiles. In Kyiv alone, six people died and 66 were injured, including three children. A 24-storey apartment block collapsed after being hit, while other buildings caught fire. The attack cut electricity to 140,000 residents, though utility workers restored power to 110,000 by morning.

In Dnipro, at least 12 people were killed and 37 injured. A three-year-old boy died when a four-storey residential building collapsed on him, and six people remain missing in the rubble. A rescuer was killed in a follow-up strike on the same location. The city's mayor accused Russia of deliberately using cluster munitions in populated areas to maximize civilian casualties.

Ukraine's air defenses intercepted approximately half the missiles fired, but more than 30 struck civilian targets. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy responded to the assault by urgently requesting Patriot missiles from the United States. He described these air defense systems as vital tools for saving lives and characterized ballistic missiles as Moscow's "last major advantage on the battlefield."

Zelenskyy said on social media: "If Ukraine is not protected from ballistic and other missile strikes, these strikes will continue. Europe needs its own anti-ballistic missiles so that this war can finally end."

The Trump administration has not yet responded to these requests despite Zelenskyy's previous pleas. Ukraine claims it is running out of Patriot interceptors, the only air defense system capable of stopping fast-moving ballistic missiles. The U.S. had recently depleted its Patriot stockpile during operations against Iran.

Ukrainian officials attribute the escalation to Russia's deteriorating military position. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated: "Putin is a war criminal and loser who has no cards except terror. Moscow is losing on the battlefield. No number of missiles can change this."

The attack followed days of Russian threats against Kyiv. Zelenskyy had warned residents on Monday that intelligence indicated a major strike was being prepared. The combination of warnings and delayed execution appeared designed to create psychological pressure on civilians.

In recent weeks, Ukraine has conducted increasingly effective long-range drone campaigns against Russian oil refineries, ports, and critical supply corridors. Military analysts suggest Russia is attempting to strengthen its negotiating position through intensified civilian attacks despite mounting battlefield losses.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Backing Down From Beirut Threat
cards.teaser: Israeli forces attacked targets in southern Lebanon hours after holding off from striking Beirut under US pressure.
cards.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu decided against attacking Beirut after pressure from President Trump. Instead, Israel carried out strikes in southern Lebanon while Netanyahu committed to continuing military operations against Hezbollah.

The conflict threatens ongoing peace negotiations involving the United States and Iran. A ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah is considered essential to the broader peace process. The White House is pushing for a deal to end the war, though Iran is seeking concessions before backing down.

cards.headline: Health Workers Battle Ebola Outbreak in War-Torn Eastern Congo
cards.teaser: Medical teams race to establish treatment centers and expand testing as Ebola spreads in a region still recovering from years of conflict.
cards.body:
Health care workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo are opening new Ebola treatment centers and expanding testing capacity as the outbreak spreads through the eastern Ituri province. The response teams face significant obstacles, working in an area destabilized by years of armed conflict where infrastructure and security remain compromised.

The outbreak involves the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, for which there is currently no approved drug or vaccine. Congo has reported over 1,000 suspected cases of the virus. Health workers must contain the disease while navigating the compounded challenges created by the ongoing conflict in the region.

cards.headline: Two Protesters Killed During Demonstrations Against US Ebola Center in Kenya
cards.teaser: Police shot two people dead as protests erupted over American plans to build an Ebola treatment facility.
cards.body:
Two people were shot dead during protests in Kenya against a proposed US-run Ebola quarantine and treatment center. The demonstrations took place near the site where the United States plans to construct the facility.

The US proposal has generated significant public anger among local residents, who have organized multiple protests against the project.

cards.headline: UK Releases Mandelson Files Linked to Epstein Ties
cards.teaser: The British government published documents related to Peter Mandelson, the former diplomat recently appointed as ambassador to Washington.
cards.body:
The United Kingdom released files concerning Peter Mandelson, a former diplomat who has connections to Jeffrey Epstein. The documents address questions about Mandelson's government work and his recent appointment to serve as the UK ambassador to the United States. A minister described the released messages as embarrassing but defended the government's overall record.

The release left several questions unanswered about Mandelson's activities and relationships. Prime Minister Starmer had prepared for the document release, which includes hundreds of messages involving the diplomat. The files shed light on both his government service and the circumstances surrounding his selection for the Washington posting.

cards.headline: Hackers Exploit Instagram AI Chatbot to Access User Accounts
cards.teaser: Security researchers tricked Instagram's artificial intelligence chatbot into providing access to user accounts.
cards.body:
Hackers successfully tricked Meta's AI support chatbot into granting access to Instagram accounts belonging to other users. The breach allowed unauthorized individuals to hijack accounts through social engineering attacks targeting the automated system.

Multiple users reported having their Instagram accounts compromised over the weekend. The incident has been linked to recent high-profile account hijackings, raising concerns about the security vulnerabilities of AI-powered customer service tools.

cards.headline: American Influencer Admits Assault at London Subway Station
cards.teaser: Melissa Rein Lively, who has a following in conservative political circles, accepted a caution for an incident on the London Underground.
cards.body:
Melissa Rein Lively, an influencer associated with conservative political movements, admitted to assault at a London Tube station. She accepted a caution from British authorities in connection with the incident.

Prosecutors withdrew a charge of assault by beating against Lively as part of the resolution. The case concludes legal proceedings stemming from the confrontation that occurred on the London transit system.

hero.headline: Trump says Iran negotiations continuing despite complexity
hero.teaser: President Trump stated that talks with Iran remain active, describing the pursuit of a deal as a complicated process.
hero.body:
President Trump told Fox News that negotiations with Iran are ongoing, characterizing the effort to reach an agreement as a difficult undertaking. He dismissed suggestions that talks had stalled, saying a deal is not a simple thing to achieve.

The comments come as Trump reviews a proposed memorandum of understanding drafted by American and Iranian diplomats with assistance from Pakistan and Qatar. The preliminary agreement would continue the current ceasefire for 60 days while negotiations continue on a more permanent peace accord. Reports indicate Tehran has suspended discussions over Israeli military actions in Lebanon, though the White House continues pushing for a deal amid polling pressure and demands from Gulf allies.

cards.headline: Russian strikes kill 18 in Ukraine, including eight-year-old boy
cards.teaser: Ukrainian rescue workers recovered bodies from rubble after attacks killed 18 people across the country.
cards.body:
Russian military strikes killed 18 people in Ukraine, with an eight-year-old boy and a woman among those who died when a strike hit an apartment block.

Rescue teams worked through the rubble of damaged buildings to recover victims. The strikes, which included hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles targeting Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, left some people trapped under the debris of apartment buildings as emergency workers continued search and recovery operations.

cards.headline: Instagram AI chatbot exploited by hackers to access user accounts
cards.teaser: Security researchers found vulnerabilities in Instagram's AI chatbot that allowed unauthorized access to accounts.
cards.body:
Hackers tricked Meta's AI support chatbot into granting access to Instagram accounts, leading to multiple account hijackings over the weekend. Several users reported their accounts had been compromised through this method.

The incident has been linked to recent cases of high-profile Instagram accounts being taken over, raising concerns about the security vulnerabilities in AI-powered customer service tools deployed by major social media platforms.

cards.headline: Former SNP chief executive admits embezzling £400,000 from party
cards.teaser: Peter Murrell used Scottish National Party credit cards for a £400,000 spending spree and faces a lengthy prison sentence.
cards.body:
Peter Murrell, the Scottish National Party's former chief executive, has admitted to embezzling £400,000 from the party. He used SNP credit cards to fund a substantial spending spree on personal expenses.

Murrell faces a lengthy prison sentence following his guilty plea. The embezzlement scandal represents one of the most significant financial breaches in the party's history.

cards.headline: UK Athletics fined £350,000 over Paralympian's death
cards.teaser: A judge imposed the penalty after equipment fell on an athlete at a training facility in east London.
cards.body:
UK Athletics was fined £350,000 plus £44,000 in costs at the Old Bailey after a paralympic athlete died when equipment fell on him at a training ground in east London.

The judge imposed the penalty following a hearing into the circumstances of the fatal incident, holding the organization responsible for the accident.

cards.headline: Student told police 'I can't breathe' while handcuffed before death
cards.teaser: Henry Nowak made the statement to officers as he was dying, according to reports on his case.
cards.body:
Murdered student Henry Nowak told police he could not breathe while handcuffed. The statement was made as he was dying.

An independent investigation is examining why police handcuffed Nowak during this period while he was in medical distress.

cards.headline: Reality TV figure Spencer Pratt in tight Los Angeles mayoral race
cards.teaser: The Republican known for his role on The Hills is competing with two Democrats for mayor of the country's second-largest city.
cards.body:
Spencer Pratt, a Republican who gained fame on the reality television show The Hills, appears to be in a close race for mayor of Los Angeles. He is running against two Democratic candidates for leadership of one of America's largest cities.

The contest represents an unusual intersection of entertainment and politics in a city long associated with both industries. Los Angeles is the second-largest city in the United States by population.

hero.headline: Investor Andrew Left Found Guilty of Securities Fraud
hero.body:
A federal jury has convicted Andrew Left, a well-known short-seller, of securities fraud charges. The verdict marks a significant moment for the investment community, particularly those who profit from betting that stock prices will decline.

Left built his reputation through Citron Research, a firm that published reports questioning the valuations and business practices of publicly traded companies. His analysis often sparked substantial movements in stock prices, attracting both supporters who agreed with his assessments and criticism from the companies he targeted.

Prosecutors charged Left with manipulating markets through his research reports and social media posts. The government argued that his public statements about companies he had shorted were designed to move stock prices in ways that benefited his positions. A jury deliberated before reaching the guilty verdict on the securities fraud charges.

The conviction carries serious potential consequences, including fines and prison time. A sentencing date has not yet been scheduled. Legal experts anticipate the case will influence how regulators and prosecutors define the boundary between legitimate critical research and illegal market manipulation.

The verdict has generated considerable concern within the short-selling community. Other investors who engage in this practice worry the conviction could establish a legal precedent that restricts their ability to publish critical research about companies. Short-selling involves borrowing shares, selling them immediately, and then purchasing them back at a lower price to profit from the difference. Practitioners in this field frequently publish detailed research explaining their negative views on target companies.

The case has drawn attention from financial analysts and legal experts who are monitoring whether the verdict leads to increased regulatory scrutiny of short-sellers' activities and publications. Many in the investment community are closely watching to see what precedent this conviction may set for their own work.

Citron Research gained prominence for its reports on various companies, sometimes making bold claims about their business models and financial health. Left's work became influential enough that his findings could trigger significant stock price movements, demonstrating the market impact his research could achieve.

The guilty verdict represents a notable moment in discussions about market manipulation and investor speech. As the legal process moves toward sentencing, observers across Wall Street are considering the implications for how short-sellers can operate and communicate their research findings to the public. The outcome may reshape how prosecutors and regulators approach cases involving investment research and stock price movements going forward.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Proposes 25% Tariff on Brazil
cards.teaser: The White House announced plans for new tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing trade practices it considers unfair.
cards.body:
President Trump proposed a 25% tariff on imports from Brazil, marking another step in the administration's use of trade barriers. The proposal cites what officials describe as unfair trade practices by Brazil.

The tariff plan relies on Section 301 investigations, a legal mechanism the administration has used to justify trade actions. The move represents the latest effort to rebuild the administration's tariff strategy following previous trade disputes.

cards.headline: Stock Futures Decline as AI Gains Meet Mideast Concerns
cards.teaser: U.S. stock futures dropped after a record-setting session, with investors weighing geopolitical developments against technology sector strength.
cards.body:
Dow futures fell following a record close on Wall Street, as markets weighed competing forces. Technology stocks remained in focus after powering the previous session's gains, with major AI companies drawing investor attention.

Major tech firms are making significant moves to capitalize on AI momentum. Anthropic plans to offer public share sales later this year as its valuation approaches $1 trillion, while Alphabet announced plans to raise up to $80 billion through equity offerings to fund AI infrastructure investments. The fundraising push included a $10 billion share purchase by Berkshire Hathaway.

cards.headline: Nvidia CEO Predicts Marvell Could Reach Trillion-Dollar Valuation
cards.teaser: Jensen Huang said Marvell Technology could join the exclusive club of companies worth over $1 trillion, sending the stock up 25%.
cards.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that Marvell Technology may become the next trillion-dollar company. Following his comments, Marvell's stock surged 25%.

Marvell specializes in connectivity technology for data centers and AI systems. The company's leadership views connectivity as a critical bottleneck in AI development, positioning Marvell's chips and technology—which link processors and systems in data centers—as essential infrastructure.

cards.headline: Victoria's Secret Raises Full-Year Outlook on Sales Growth
cards.teaser: The lingerie retailer increased its financial guidance after first-quarter results beat expectations, driven by gains in customer base and market share.
cards.body:
Victoria's Secret boosted its outlook for the year after reporting stronger-than-expected sales in the first quarter of 2026. The company said it expects total sales to surpass $7 billion as it continues to attract customers and gain market share. Bra sales have powered the turnaround.

The retailer beat earnings expectations for the quarter and raised its full-year guidance. Victoria's Secret has worked to rebuild its brand and customer base in recent years. The company reported growth in both customer numbers and the share of the market it captures.

cards.headline: Hackers Trick Instagram AI Chatbot to Access User Accounts
cards.teaser: Security researchers demonstrated vulnerabilities in Instagram's AI assistant that allowed unauthorized access to accounts.
cards.body:
Hackers exploited Meta's AI support chatbot to gain unauthorized access to Instagram accounts. Multiple users reported having their accounts hijacked over the weekend after the chatbot granted attackers entry credentials.

The incident sparked connections to recent high-profile Instagram account takeovers. The breach demonstrates vulnerabilities in AI systems designed to handle account recovery and security requests, raising concerns about deploying artificial intelligence with access to sensitive user authentication processes.

cards.headline: One-Third of People Say University Degree Not Worth Cost
cards.teaser: British lawmakers opened an inquiry into student debt as surveys show growing doubt about the value of higher education.
cards.body:
A third of people believe a university degree does not justify its cost, according to surveys released as British MPs launched an inquiry into student loans. Graduates have expressed concerns about the size of their debts and the interest rates charged on student borrowing.

Parliament will hear testimony from graduates about their experiences with student loan repayment. The inquiry reflects growing uncertainty about whether higher education represents good value for money.

hero.headline: Rocket engine startup Impulse raises $500 million in funding round
hero.body:
Impulse Space announced it has secured $500 million in new funding, marking one of the larger capital raises in the commercial space sector this year.

The company develops rocket engine technology and space propulsion systems for satellites and spacecraft. President Eric Romo stated that the company intends to use the capital to expand its workforce rather than invest heavily in artificial intelligence systems for engineering tasks.

Romo indicated that designing and building physical systems like rocket engines still requires human expertise that cannot yet be effectively replaced by AI. The engineering work involved in developing propulsion technology demands hands-on problem solving and judgment that current automation systems cannot adequately replicate.

Impulse Space operates in a competitive landscape alongside established aerospace contractors and numerous space startups, all working to advance propulsion capabilities and reduce launch costs. The commercial space sector has attracted billions in venture capital investment over recent years as companies pursue increasingly ambitious goals in orbit operations.

The company's decision to prioritize human hiring stands in contrast to broader technology industry trends. Many sectors have increasingly turned to AI to reduce headcount or automate technical work. However, Romo's position reflects a view held by many in the aerospace and engineering sectors that complex physical systems require expertise that goes beyond current AI capabilities.

The funding round comes as competition intensifies in the space propulsion market. Companies are racing to develop technologies that will support a growing range of space missions, from satellite deployments to deep space exploration. Access to capital has become crucial for startups attempting to bridge the gap between initial development and commercial operations.

Impulse Space has not disclosed its current employee count or specified how many new workers it plans to hire with the fresh funding. The company also has not announced specific timelines for upcoming product launches or testing schedules following this funding round.

The investment reflects investor confidence in Impulse Space's technology and business model, even as the broader space industry continues to consolidate and mature. Venture capital firms have increasingly focused on companies developing core infrastructure and propulsion capabilities, seeing these as essential technologies for the expanding commercial space economy.

As the company moves forward, it will face ongoing pressure to demonstrate progress toward operational milestones. The funding provides resources to accelerate development work, but success in the space sector ultimately depends on achieving reliable, cost-effective propulsion systems that meet market demands.

cards.headline: Pacific Fusion prototype delivers 440 gigawatts in 80-nanosecond burst
cards.teaser: A fusion energy company tested a prototype that produced enormous power output in a fraction of a second.
cards.body:
Pacific Fusion's sub-scale prototype successfully delivered 440 gigawatts of power in an 80-nanosecond burst. This achievement marks progress toward the company's goal of building a demonstration power plant.

The intense power output in such a brief timeframe validates Pacific Fusion's technical approach to fusion energy generation, which relies on fusing atomic nuclei under extreme conditions to produce electricity.

cards.headline: ZeroDrift raises $10 million for AI compliance monitoring service
cards.teaser: A startup has raised funding to develop technology that screens AI-generated messages for compliance issues.
cards.body:
ZeroDrift has raised $10 million to build an AI compliance service that operates between AI models and their end users. The platform flags and replaces messages that could create compliance issues, monitoring AI outputs in real time to catch content that might violate regulations or company policies.

The funding supports the company's platform development as businesses face growing pressure to responsibly deploy AI systems that interact with customers and process sensitive information.

cards.headline: NASA rover captures high-resolution panorama of Mars surface
cards.teaser: The Perseverance rover photographed one of the sharpest wide-angle views of the Martian landscape.
cards.body:
NASA's Perseverance rover captured a striking panoramic image of Mars during clear atmospheric conditions, producing one of the sharpest wide-angle views of the planet's surface recorded by the rover.

The rover also took a new selfie on Mars. Both Perseverance and Curiosity continue their exploration of different Martian regions, collecting data that helps scientists understand the planet's geological history spanning billions of years.

cards.headline: Fish species survives 100,000 years without males
cards.teaser: Scientists studied a fish species that has reproduced without males for millennia and found it thriving rather than declining.
cards.body:
A fish species has survived for 100,000 years without males, according to research. Scientists had expected the species to have died out due to lack of genetic diversity that typically comes from sexual reproduction.

The species is thriving despite the theoretical disadvantages of reproducing without males. The finding challenges assumptions about the long-term viability of asexual reproduction in vertebrate animals.

cards.headline: Water voles reintroduced to Farnham river after 20-year absence
cards.teaser: About 300 water voles were released into a river system as part of an effort to restore the species.
cards.body:
Conservationists released approximately 300 water voles in Farnham as part of a project to bring the species back to the river. Water voles had been absent from the area for 20 years.

The release is part of a broader effort to restore water vole populations, which have declined significantly in many areas. The species faces threats from habitat loss and predation by non-native mink.

cards.headline: Rosetta probe found life-building chemicals in comet's atmosphere
cards.teaser: The European Space Agency's Rosetta mission detected chemical ingredients around a comet that may have helped life begin on Earth.
cards.body:
The Rosetta spacecraft detected organic compounds in the atmosphere surrounding Comet 67P. Analysis of the gas cloud revealed hydrogen sulfide, ammonia, and hydrogen cyanide—chemicals that would create a distinctive odor combining rotten eggs, ammonia, and bitter almonds.

Scientists believe these chemical compounds could have played a role in the origins of life on Earth. The discovery supports the theory that comets may have delivered essential organic molecules to our planet through impacts billions of years ago.

hero.headline: Hall of Fame basketball coach Rick Adelman dies at 79
hero.body:
Rick Adelman, a Hall of Fame basketball coach who compiled more than 1,000 victories during his three decades in the NBA, has died at 79. His career spanned from 1988 to 2014, during which he coached the Portland Trail Blazers, Sacramento Kings, Houston Rockets, and Minnesota Timberwolves.

Adelman became recognized for his innovative offensive strategies and his talent for developing players across his time with multiple franchises. He led the Trail Blazers to two NBA Finals appearances in 1990 and 1992, though the team was unable to win a championship in either year. His tenure with the Kings in the early 2000s showcased some of the era's most impressive offensive basketball, establishing Sacramento as a consistent playoff competitor under his leadership.

Throughout his coaching career, Adelman won 1,042 regular season games, placing him among the top 10 coaches in NBA history in that category. The Basketball Hall of Fame recognized his lasting success and his influence on professional basketball by inducting him. Many players who played for Adelman spoke about how his confidence in their abilities and his mentorship shaped their development as athletes.

Before becoming a coach, Adelman played as a guard in the NBA. He moved into coaching after his playing career concluded and eventually worked his way up to become a head coach. He established himself as one of the most respected coaches in professional basketball through his sustained success and leadership.

Adelman's coaching approach focused on ball movement and proper spacing on the court, principles that have grown increasingly important in modern basketball. His strategic insights helped shape how the game is played today.

The basketball community has responded to his passing by sharing stories of his character and his impact as a coach. People who worked with him during his time coaching the Kings, Trail Blazers, and other teams have highlighted his humanity and the ways he influenced both the careers and personal lives of his players.

Adelman's career achievements place him among the most successful coaches in basketball history. His ability to sustain excellence across different organizations and his commitment to developing talent earned him respect throughout the sport. The coaches and players who worked under him credited his guidance as instrumental in their success both during and after their time on the court.

His death represents a significant loss for the basketball community, which has long recognized him as one of the game's greatest coaches and most influential figures in shaping modern basketball strategy and player development.

cards.headline: Kenny Dalglish undergoing treatment for cancer
cards.teaser: The Scotland, Liverpool, and Celtic great confirmed he is receiving treatment for cancer.
cards.body:
Sir Kenny Dalglish has confirmed he is undergoing treatment for cancer. The Scotland, Liverpool and Celtic legend is one of football's greatest figures, having achieved remarkable success across his playing and managerial career.

Dalglish is widely regarded among the sport's all-time greats, with an extraordinary legacy spanning multiple clubs and numerous honours.

cards.headline: UK Athletics fined £350,000 over death of Paralympian
cards.teaser: A judge imposed the fine after a Paralympic athlete died when equipment fell on him at a training ground in east London.
cards.body:
UK Athletics has been fined £350,000 with £44,000 in costs by a judge at the Old Bailey. The penalties follow the death of a Paralympic athlete who was struck by equipment at a training ground in east London.

The judge imposed the financial penalties after hearing evidence about the circumstances of the fatal incident at the facility.

cards.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams
cards.teaser: The Cleveland Browns traded defensive star Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams for Jared Verse and three draft picks.
cards.body:
The Cleveland Browns have traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks. Garrett, 30, is a two-time Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since being drafted first overall by Cleveland in 2017, he has recorded 125.5 sacks, 413 pressures and 149 tackles for loss—the most of any player during that span. In 2025, he set an NFL single-season sacks record with 23.

The trade marks a significant roster move for the Rams, who add one of the league's premier defensive talents to their roster.

cards.headline: Eagles trade A.J. Brown to Patriots
cards.teaser: Philadelphia agreed to send wide receiver A.J. Brown to New England for two draft picks, including a 2028 first-round selection.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots. In return, the Eagles will receive a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowl selection, had grown frustrated with the Eagles organization.

The trade reunites Brown with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and ends months of speculation about his future in Philadelphia. Both teams announced the deal on Monday.

cards.headline: Liverpool in advanced talks with Andoni Iraola
cards.teaser: The club is pursuing Iraola as its next head coach following the dismissal of Arne Slot.
cards.body:
Liverpool are in advanced talks with Andoni Iraola to become their new head coach, following Arne Slot's sacking on Saturday. The Spaniard is the clear frontrunner for the position.

Iraola's style of play aligns with Liverpool's desire for a front-footed, aggressive approach, which the club felt was missing during Slot's second season. Liverpool aim to complete the appointment before the World Cup begins.

cards.headline: Fulham coach Marco Silva close to Benfica agreement
cards.teaser: Silva is nearing a deal to leave Fulham and take charge at the Portuguese club.
cards.body:
Fulham head coach Marco Silva is close to reaching an agreement to take charge at Benfica. The move would see Silva return to Portugal, where he previously worked before taking positions in England.

Silva has been managing Fulham in the Premier League but appears set to depart for Benfica. The agreement between the Portuguese club and Silva is reportedly near completion, though Fulham will need to find a replacement once the deal is finalized.

hero.headline: Sabrina Carpenter Receives Restraining Order After Man Appears at Her Home
hero.body:
Pop singer Sabrina Carpenter has obtained a restraining order against a man who appeared at her Los Angeles home after reporting a series of deeply alarming incidents to police.

The 26-year-old artist, who has achieved significant success with recent hits including "Espresso" and "Please Please Please," reported the encounters to Los Angeles law enforcement, who investigated the matter. The restraining order was granted as a legal response to the unwanted contact.

A restraining order serves as a protective legal measure that prohibits an individual from approaching or contacting the protected person. In cases involving public figures, these orders establish specific boundaries and define consequences for violations. Typically, such orders specify the minimum distance the restrained person must maintain from the protected individual and their residence.

While the exact details of the incidents remain undisclosed, law enforcement handled the investigation and the restraining order was subsequently obtained. The identity of the individual subject to the order has not been publicly revealed.

Carpenter has maintained a prominent public profile throughout her career as a recording artist and former actress. Her recent musical output has solidified her position among contemporary pop's most successful performers. Beyond her chart success, she has become known for her engaging live performances and prolific output across multiple projects.

Security concerns represent an ongoing challenge for celebrities whose public visibility can attract unwanted attention. High-profile individuals frequently face incidents involving unauthorized contact at their homes and other private locations. Restraining orders provide one legal tool available to entertainers seeking to protect their safety and privacy while continuing their public careers.

The situation adds to broader discussions about celebrity safety in an era where social media and public accessibility create new vulnerabilities. Public figures must balance their professional need for visibility and connection with fans against the practical necessity of maintaining secure personal spaces. Many entertainers have pursued similar legal protections when experiencing threatening or disturbing contact.

For performers like Carpenter who maintain active touring schedules and significant media presence, security measures have become standard practice. The restraining order represents a formal legal boundary designed to deter further unwanted contact and provide recourse if violations occur.

The incident reflects patterns seen across the entertainment industry where unauthorized home visits and persistent unwanted contact have prompted celebrities to seek legal intervention. Such protective orders remain one of the primary mechanisms available to address these security challenges while allowing public figures to continue their work in the entertainment field.

cards.headline: Fab Morvan Withdraws From Freedom 250 Concerts After Trump Criticism
cards.teaser: The Milli Vanilli member reversed his earlier commitment to perform at the Washington concerts following remarks from former President Trump about participating artists.
cards.body:
Fab Morvan of Milli Vanilli announced he will not perform at the Freedom 250 concerts in Washington, reversing his previous commitment to the event. His withdrawal followed a tirade from Trump directed at artists scheduled to appear at the concerts.

Morvan initially said he was eager to perform alongside Vanilla Ice, who remained one of the two artists still committed to the event out of nine originally booked. With Morvan's departure, Vanilla Ice appears to be the sole performer still planning to participate in the Freedom 250 concerts.

cards.headline: Rosamund Pike Confronts Audience Member for Texting During West End Play
cards.teaser: The actress called out someone for using their phone during the climactic scene of Inter Alia, the performance that earned her an Olivier Award in April.
cards.body:
Rosamund Pike called out an audience member for texting during a climactic scene of her West End play "Inter Alia," directly addressing them with the words "you know who you are." The incident highlighted the ongoing issue of phone use disrupting live theater performances.

Pike's role in the production earned her an Olivier award in April. "Inter Alia" centers on Jessica Parks, a crown court judge who confronts the legal system's handling of sexual violence while navigating her own personal challenges.

cards.headline: BTS and Cardi B to Headline iHeartRadio Music Festival in September
cards.teaser: The two-night event at Las Vegas T-Mobile Arena will feature performances by BTS, Cardi B, Benson Boone, and other major acts.
cards.body:
The iHeartRadio Music Festival, presented by Capital One, will take place on September 18 and 19 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. Ryan Seacrest will host the event, which features a lineup spanning multiple genres.

In addition to BTS, Cardi B, and Benson Boone, the festival will include performances from Goo Goo Dolls, Kenny Chesney, Lainey Wilson, Major Lazer, Muse, and Snoop Dogg. The annual music festival brings together artists from pop, hip-hop, country, and rock for the two-day celebration.

cards.headline: Michelle Obama Names Dave Chappelle as Favorite Guest on Her Podcast
cards.teaser: The former First Lady praised the comedian as one of the smartest people on the planet during a live recording of her IMO podcast at SXSW London.
cards.body:
Michelle Obama identified comedian Dave Chappelle as one of the favorite guests on her IMO podcast during a live recording at SXSW London. She described Chappelle as one of the smartest people on the planet.

Obama co-hosts the podcast with her brother Craig Robinson. During the event, they discussed their career paths and their entry into podcasting. Obama said she never expected to become a podcast host, but has embraced the role alongside her brother in the show that explores various topics through conversation.

cards.headline: Cara Delevingne Links New Music to Sobriety Journey
cards.teaser: The model and actress released her first two songs, drawing inspiration from her experience getting sober.
cards.body:
Cara Delevingne has entered the music industry with the release of her first two songs. The model and actress said her new music was inspired by her journey to sobriety.

Delevingne has built a career spanning modeling and acting before expanding into music. Her songs mark a new creative direction for the British entertainer, who has spoken publicly about personal challenges and recovery in recent years.

cards.headline: Ranveer Singh Exit From Don 3 Sparks Major Bollywood Dispute
cards.teaser: The actor's December departure from the film triggered an industry standoff involving around 25 senior Bollywood figures and a Big Four audit.
cards.body:
Ranveer Singh walked away from Don 3 in December 2025, setting off what has become one of Bollywood's most closely watched industry disputes in years. The conflict has drawn in approximately 25 senior figures from the film business.

The dispute has escalated to include a Big Four audit and has wound through the Producers Guild. Singh is one of Bollywood's top actors, and his exit from the high-profile project has created ripples throughout the Indian film industry. The standoff represents a rare public clash among major players in Bollywood's typically private business dealings.

hero.headline: Trump administration officials address slush fund controversy
hero.teaser: Trump officials are working to calm Republican anger over a controversial Anti-Weaponization Fund that has stalled an immigration enforcement bill.
hero.body:
President Donald Trump may need to explicitly renounce his controversial Anti-Weaponization Fund before Republicans move forward with a stalled immigration enforcement bill. Trump administration officials are attempting to address the fury among congressional Republicans over the fund.

The fund, created following Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS over leaked tax return documents, establishes nearly $1.8 billion to be distributed to alleged victims of what the administration calls "lawfare." The justice department will administer the fund through four commissioners appointed by Trump's attorney general, plus one commissioner selected in consultation with congressional leadership. Trump retains the ability to fire the commissioners, giving him ultimate control over the fund's operations.

The fund will have authority to issue formal apologies for alleged mistreatment of conservative political figures by previous administrations. Legal experts and congressional critics from both parties have attacked the fund as a corrupt scheme they describe as a slush fund for Trump allies. Some have noted that January 6 insurrectionists may be eligible recipients, with some reportedly planning to apply for grants.

The controversy highlights significant tensions within the Republican party over the administration's financial priorities and use of federal resources. Some Republicans are demanding clarity on the fund before proceeding with other legislative initiatives. The dispute has become a roadblock to advancing immigration enforcement legislation that party members otherwise support.

Critics have raised concerns about the fund's lack of transparency. The fund's work is not required to be made public, and reports to the attorney general regarding its conduct must remain confidential. This opacity has drawn additional scrutiny from lawmakers concerned about accountability.

The agreement establishing the fund requires the IRS to drop all audits of Trump and his family. The justice department said it "disagrees strongly" with a recent court decision halting the fund's establishment, signaling the administration intends to continue defending the arrangement through legal channels.

Legal scholars have characterized the fund as problematic on multiple levels. They argue that because Trump effectively controlled both sides of the lawsuit against the IRS, a genuine conflict did not exist. A federal judge had commissioned an independent legal review, which found "reason to believe that the president is, in fact, exercising his control over the defendants in this litigation." The agreement was reached shortly before the judge's deadline requiring the parties to explain how they were actually in conflict.

The fund's establishment is part of a broader pattern that critics say demonstrates widespread self-dealing and conflicts of interest within the Trump administration. Beyond this particular controversy, legal experts worry the fund sets a problematic precedent for future administrations regarding the use of federal resources for personal or political purposes.

cards.headline: Rubio testifies before Senate as Iran negotiations stall
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on the State Department budget request as negotiations to end the three-m.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee on Tuesday morning regarding the State Department budget request. The hearing took place as negotiations to end the three-month war in Iran have stalled. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin also appeared before Congress for budget hearings.

Rubio addressed lawmakers on the administration's approach to the Iran conflict and its broader foreign policy priorities during the proceedings.

cards.headline: Dr. Oz to lead White House press briefing
cards.teaser: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services administrator will become the latest Trump official to fill in for press secretary Karoline during her maternity leave.
cards.body:
Dr. Mehmet Oz, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services administrator, will host the White House press briefing. He becomes the latest Trump administration official to fill in for press secretary Karoline while she is on maternity leave.

Oz follows Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Vice President JD Vance, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in leading briefings during Karoline's absence. The rotation of cabinet-level officials to the podium represents a departure from typical White House communications practices.

cards.headline: Koch-backed PAC launches Senate advertising campaign including Montana
cards.teaser: Americans for Prosperity Action began its first major Senate ad buy, coming weeks after warning the Republican Senate majority is at risk.
cards.body:
A Koch-aligned political action committee launched its first significant Senate advertising campaign, with Montana among the targeted states. The ads come from Americans for Prosperity Action, which recently warned that the Republican Senate majority faces potential threats.

The advertising buy represents an early investment in Senate races ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. The inclusion of Montana suggests the PAC views that seat as particularly competitive or important to maintaining Republican control of the chamber.

cards.headline: Mike Pence targets populism in new book on conservatism
cards.teaser: The former vice president aims to restore traditional conservatism in a Republican Party increasingly defined by Trump and populist policies.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Mike Pence sees a new calling in restoring traditional conservatism in the Republican Party. In his new book released today, What Conservatives Believe, Pence takes sharp aim at what he views as the party's drift from its core principles.

The effort represents a significant challenge in a Republican Party that is defined by President Trump, whom Pence once helped elevate, and increasingly embracing populist policies. Pence's book comes as he positions himself as a defender of conventional conservative ideology against what he characterizes as progressive influences within the GOP.

cards.headline: Smuggling tunnel discovered between San Diego and Tijuana
cards.teaser: Mexican authorities say the tunnel was used as a storage, logistics, and trafficking center for weapons, explosives and illegal drugs.
cards.body:
Mexican authorities discovered a smuggling tunnel connecting San Diego and Tijuana. Officials said the tunnel was used as a storage, logistics, and trafficking center for weapons, explosives and illegal drugs.

The discovery highlights the ongoing challenge of cross-border smuggling operations that utilize underground passages to evade detection. Such tunnels have been a recurring problem along the U.S.-Mexico border, often featuring sophisticated construction and ventilation systems.

cards.headline: Primary elections underway in six states
cards.teaser: Voters in California, Iowa, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico and South Dakota are casting ballots in 2026 primary contests.
cards.body:
Voters in California, Iowa, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico and South Dakota are casting ballots in primary elections Tuesday. The results will determine which candidates advance to the general election in November.

California's governor's race is drawing particular attention, with the state using a top-two primary system. Beyond the gubernatorial contest, several other high-stakes races are unfolding across the state, including congressional seats and local offices. Both parties are using these primaries to build momentum ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress and numerous state offices.
